incident.title: Widespread customer sign-in failures
incident.alert_or_symptom: Most new customer sign-in attempts are failing, while customers with existing authenticated sessions remain signed in.

technical_evidence.observation: Successful token issuance fell from 99.7 percent to 8.4 percent at 11:18 across the United Kingdom and Ireland storefronts.
New sign-in requests are ending with a generic authentication timeout after 30 seconds. The log entry does not identify a failing downstream component or configuration item.
The Application Compute Cluster, Transaction Database Cluster, Public API Gateway and DNS, CDN and Load-Balancing Platform are healthy and operating normally.
Customers with existing authenticated sessions can continue using the service, but most signed-out customers cannot establish a new session.

service_impact.user_impact_description: Most signed-out customers cannot authenticate, although existing sessions continue to function.

environmental_context: The Identity and Access Service supports customer authentication for the public storefronts.
No specific dependency, platform or configuration failure has been identified.
reported_unknowns: It has not been confirmed whether every authentication path and client type is affected.
No approved sign-in workaround has yet been confirmed for signed-out customers.
additional_context: No data loss, account compromise or serious security exposure has been observed.

model_output.incident_summary: Most signed-out customers cannot authenticate, while existing sessions remain active. The authentication service is experiencing a significant failure, with token issuance success rate dropping sharply.

severity.rationale: The incident involves a widespread failure of the authentication service, impacting nearly all signed-out customers. While existing sessions remain active, this is a critical business function outage.

incident_category.rationale: The primary symptom is the complete inability of most signed-out customers to authenticate, which directly indicates a service availability issue.

affected_area.rationale: The authentication service is the primary area affected, with dependencies on compute and database clusters.

routing.rationale: The primary resolver group is RG-IAM, responsible for the Identity and Access Service. RG-OPS should be coordinated due to the critical nature of the incident.
